name: IntuiExtend
author: CIERP Philippe

provenance.from: aminet dev/amos/intuiextend16.lha, held in the corpus at sources/aminet-dev-amos/files/intuiextend16/extentions/amospro/. A real library: 22,508 bytes of code.
provenance.note: The archive ships BOTH builds, `extentions/amospro/AMOSPro_IntuiExtend.lib` (294 keywords, this entry) and `extentions/amos/AMOS_IntuiExtend.Lib` (269, vendored beside it and NOT registered -- a third distinct table, for AMOS 1.3). It also carries a `bonus/easylife/` directory holding somebody else's extension, which is why a filename search for EasyLife finds hits under this one. The $VER is a keyfile line rather than a version banner: `To CIERP Philippe, IntuiExtend.lib v1.6`, the author's own registered copy.
provenance.redistribution: Aminet distribution terms unverified. Kept as a fixture for identification and reference only.

findings: 294 keywords. REGISTERED SEPARATELY FROM 2.01b ON PURPOSE, and this is the case worth understanding: the two releases share most of their keyword NAMES and almost none of their IDS -- 45 of these 294 entries are still where 2.01b puts them. An id is a byte offset into the token table, so a later release that only appends keywords leaves the earlier ones alone and one registry entry can cover both, which is how turbo-plus-1.9 covers TURBO 1.5, 1.6 and 1.11. This table was REBUILT instead, so a program saved against 1.6 and read against 2.01b resolves almost every keyword to the wrong one. src/cli/libcat.ts calls that `renumbered` and this pair is what the verdict was added for. The AMOS 1.3 build in the same archive is a third table again, 269 keywords, and is vendored unregistered. Nothing is ported.
notes: Version 1.6 fallback for IntuiExtend. Its token ids barely overlap 2.01b's, so the two cannot stand in for each other.
